Sauna and Blood Pressure

In a 2018 study of 102 adults, a 30-minute traditional sauna session at about 163°F lowered average blood pressure from 137/82 to 130/75 mmHg, and systolic pressure was still lower 30 minutes later. In a Finnish study that followed 1,621 men for a median of 24.7 years, 4 to 7 sessions a week was linked to about half the risk of developing high blood pressure. That is an association, not proof, and people with uncontrolled blood pressure should check with a doctor first.
